rubric.why: Recognises the key condition that velocity is a vector quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying velocity as a vector quantity; accept an equivalent statement that velocity has magnitude and direction.

rubric.why: Identifies the possible ways a force can change velocity.
rubric.description: The change may be in magnitude, direction, or both.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the change can be in magnitude and direction, or in both.

modelAnswer: As velocity is a vector quantity, so the change may be in its magnitude, direction or in both of them.

rubric.why: The law applies unless an external force acts on the body.
rubric.description: The body is not acted upon by an external force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the external-force condition. Accept an equivalent condition that no external force acts.

rubric.why: States the body's motion that persists under the law.
rubric.description: A body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that rest continues, or that uniform motion in a straight line continues.

modelAnswer: A body continues its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by some external force.

rubric.why: Identifies that impulse concerns a force acting for a short duration.
rubric.description: A large force acts for a short interval of time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning a force acting over a short time interval.

rubric.why: Gives the defining quantity for impulse.
rubric.description: Impulse is the total change in the object's momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining impulse as the change in momentum.

modelAnswer: When a large force F acts on an object for a short interval of time, the impulse of the force is defined as the total change in momentum of the object.

rubric.why: Identifies that the vehicle starts moving suddenly from rest.
rubric.description: The car starts moving quickly from rest.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the vehicle suddenly starts or accelerates from rest.

rubric.why: Explains the backward push using the passengers' tendency to remain at rest.
rubric.description: Passengers tend to retain their state of rest and are pushed back against the seat.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for attributing the effect to the tendency to remain at rest or to inertia.

modelAnswer: On the other hand, when the bus starts moving quickly from rest, the passengers are pushed back against the seat. This time, the tendency of passengers is to retain their state of rest.

rubric.why: Identifies the constant nature of the velocity.
rubric.description: The object achieves a constant velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the object reaches a constant velocity.

rubric.description: This constant velocity is called terminal velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming it terminal velocity.

modelAnswer: This constant velocity achieved by an object is called its terminal velocity.

rubric.why: States the condition under which momentum is conserved.
rubric.description: No external force acts on an isolated system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the system is isolated or that no external force acts.

rubric.why: States that total momentum remains unchanged.
rubric.description: The final total momentum equals the initial total momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that final momentum equals initial momentum.

modelAnswer: If no external force acts on an isolated system, the final total momentum of the system is equal to the initial total momentum of the system.

rubric.description: Names at least two contact forces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct examples from friction, drag, thrust, normal force and air resistance.

rubric.why: Completes the requested list of five contact-force examples.
rubric.description: Names the remaining examples to give all five: friction, drag, thrust, normal force and air resistance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a list containing all five correct examples in total.

modelAnswer: Friction, drag, thrust, normal force and air resistance.
